Image 1 is the first frame of the clip and image 2 is the last frame. Her left hand at the card shoe draws the yellow card up out of the opening, holding it by its short end between thumb and fingers, and carries it low over the table to its place in front of her, where the last frame shows it. On the way her wrist rolls once and hand and card turn over together about the card's long side, like turning a key: the broad yellow side narrows to a thin edge, then the broad blue side opens upward. With the same hold she lays the card flat at its place, blue side up, and her fingertips come to rest on it, as in the last frame. She is alive and attentive: her eyes follow the card the whole way, her head turns with it from the shoe to the middle of the table, and her shoulder and upper body lean slightly with the reach, naturally, as a professional dealer moves. She blinks once. Her other hand rests on the table and does not move. Only one card moves: a small card, about half as long as her hand, which keeps the same size all the way. It is blank, solid yellow on one side and solid blue on the other. The next card in the shoe is the same blank yellow. Her hands stay small and slender, the same size as in the first frame, with the same tattoos. The black card shoe does not move. The background stays the same flat green everywhere: no table is visible, there are no shadows on the green, and nothing else appears. No sound.
